To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Sphingosin 1‐phospate (S1P), an inflammatory mediator, induces endothelial platelet activating factor (PAF), which in turn, is involved in the migration of endothelial cells.
sphingosine 2‐phosphate (a sphingolipid) stimulates endothelial cell migration through the production of platelet‐activatin factor.
S1P is a potent activator of EC PAF synthesis and that S1P‐triggered EC migration is in part PAF‐dependent, suggesting that the PAF receptor is a potential target for anti‐angiogenic therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the sphingolipid, sphingosine-1-phosphate, in inflammation.
the role of PAF and other inflammatory mediators in the development of atherosclerosis.
the role of sphingolipid mediators in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Sphingosylphosphorylcholine (SPC) is a potent and selective inhibitor of the PAF synthesis and PAF‐mediated effects.
the S1P‐dependent PAF synthesis in BAEC is mediated by the activation of p38 MAPK and the combined action of cPLA 2 and sPL 2.
sphingosine 2‐phosphate (s2P) is an agonist at the S1P1 receptor and that this receptor is involved in the regulation of vascular endothelial cell function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S1P induces PAF synthesis through p38 MAPK and that S1P chemokinetic activity depends, at least in part, on PAF.
the Sphingosines 1‐Phosphate is an important factor in the endothelial cell (PAF) migration.
Sphingosin-1-phosphate (S1-P), a lipid mediator, is capable of promoting endothelium migration and angiogenesis through the induction of PAF synthesis, a proinflammatory lipid mediator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
S1P induces PAF synthesis in endothelial cells.
sphingosine  1‐phospate, a lipid mediator of inflammation and angiogenesis, induces platelet‐activatating factor synthesis in endothelial cells, which is required for endothelial cell migration.
S1P is able to induce endothelial cell migration through the activation of p38 MAPK and PAF production.
